parts.name: The Teardown
parts.pain: You don’t know yet if an audit is worth $500.
parts.promise: Three fixes, free, on one screenshot.
steps: The three things I’d fix first, marked on a screenshot of your site or app
For each one: what’s wrong, why it costs you, and the fix
No call and no pitch. If it’s useful, you’ll know what the audit is like

parts.name: The Audit
parts.pain: You can tell something’s off. You can’t tell what.
parts.promise: Everything that’s costing you users, ranked.
steps: I walk your key flows as a first-time visitor: first visit, sign-up, the core action, upgrade and checkout
Desktop and mobile
Every issue ranked by how much it affects whether people trust you, start and pay
Quick wins you can ship the same day
A part map: which of parts 02 to 07 you need
Visitor tracking set up with you on day 1, in an account you own, so a baseline builds before anything changes
Delivered within 24 hours of getting your app details. At least 10 fixes worth making, or your money back

parts.name: The First Screen
parts.pain: Visitors leave before they know what you do.
parts.promise: They get it at first glance.
steps: A headline that says what you sell, with everything under it in order of importance
One primary button, where people look for it
A navbar laid out the way visitors expect: logo left, links center, account actions right
A demo that shows one thing in full, so people want to try their own

parts.name: The Way In
steps: A short welcome flow, so people know what’s coming
A first-login walkthrough that says what each part of the app is for
Step counts and transitions in every multi-step flow
Loading and empty states, so no screen is ever blank

parts.name: The Core Action
parts.pain: The main thing works, but it doesn’t feel trustworthy.
parts.promise: The thing they came for feels good to use.
steps: Features that don’t work yet, hidden until they do
Buttons that look like buttons and links that look like links. Nothing looks clickable unless it is
Screens grouped around the job people came to do, not around features
Each person sees only the screens their role needs

parts.name: The Money Page
steps: The plan you want people to buy, shown first
Every discount shown against the price it comes off
Fine print and cancel buttons moved off the sales page
One clear line on what happens to their data
An upgrade button in the app that’s always in reach

parts.name: The System
parts.pain: Every screen looks like it came from a different app, because each prompt made it from scratch.
steps: One type scale, one spacing scale, and colors with a job: brand color on the main action, neutral on the rest
Consistent components: buttons, inputs, cards, and tags as pills
Contrast checked on every surface
A design-rules file for Lovable, Cursor or Claude, so the next screens they make match

parts.name: The Edges
parts.pain: It works, but it feels unfinished.
steps: Mobile layouts that fit the screen, with no sideways scrolling
Motion between steps and screens
Designed error, loading and empty states instead of the defaults
The small things fixed: footers that stop short, borders that flash, missing focus states

parts.name: The Re-Audit
parts.pain: You paid for fixes. How do you know they all shipped?
steps: I run the day-1 audit again on what shipped
Every finding marked fixed, with a before and after
A first scorecard from your visitor data: how many people make it through each key flow, before and after
Anything still open, I fix for free
A handover: what changed, and how to keep it that way

parts.name: The Keep
parts.pain: You ship a new feature and it breaks the look.
parts.promise: It stays good as you ship.
steps: New screens reviewed before they go live
UI fixes shipped as they come up
A short audit and a visitor scorecard every month
Your design-rules file kept up to date

cases.name: WellNest
cases.summary: A health tracker for people living with chronic illness, built in Base44. Its founder asked for feedback on Reddit, so I sent a free teardown.

before.alt: WellNest’s homepage before: floating cards cover the paragraph, a waitlist sits under the main button, and two “FREE” pills sit beside the price. Each is marked with a red number.
before.caption: Before · the teardown, numbered to match the fixes below

after.alt: WellNest’s homepage after: the floating cards sit clear of the text, one line explains the price, and the trial is the only sign-up.
after.caption: After · the same screen, once the fixes were live

fixes.found: On a laptop, the floating preview cards landed on the headline and the paragraph.
fixes.shipped: The cards moved to the sides, clear of the text.

fixes.found: A waitlist for a feature that wasn’t out yet sat right under the main button.
fixes.shipped: The free trial is the only sign-up on the first screen.

fixes.found: Two “FREE” pills beside “From AU$4.99/month” left people guessing what was free.
fixes.shipped: One plain line: free for 7 days, then AU$4.99 a month.

fixes.found: The link for people managing more than one condition was dark green on near-black, at 1.9:1 contrast.
fixes.shipped: Light text at 14:1. Readable text needs 4.5:1.

fixes.found: In the free preview, the pain slider started at 5 but said “Not selected”, so tapping 5 did nothing.
